name: Dong Drum Towers and Wind-Rain Bridges
summary: Distinctive wooden structures built by Dong people featuring multi-tiered towers and covered bridges.
description: Elaborate wooden drum towers with multiple tiers without nails and covered wind-rain bridges with elaborate pavilions, serving as community centers and gathering places. Developed by Dong people as architectural expressions of their cultural identity and social organization.
culturalContext: The Dong people's drum towers and wind-rain bridges — Guizhou, Guangxi, Hunan (Chengyang's Yongji Bridge is the icon) — build mortise-and-tenon timber cities without nails: multi-tier drum towers (drum court, fire hearth, up to 17 stacked eaves), covered bridges whose corridors shelter markets and rest, and canal-set village plans linking water, paddy and clan squares. Dong carpenters (bigsu) transmit the craft orally; the structures are UNESCO intangible-heritage celebrated and China's most photographed wooden vernacular.
